stem:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change
$Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2e^- \rightarrow Fe(s) + 2OH^-(aq) \quad E^\theta = -0.88\text{ V}$
and $AgBr(s) + e^- \rightarrow Ag(s) + Br^-(aq) \quad E^\theta = +0.07\text{ V}$
Which of the following option is correct?
options: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell
solution:
For a spontaneous cell reaction, $E_{cell}^\theta > 0$. Therefore, the half-cell with the higher standard reduction potential undergoes reduction (acts as the cathode), and the other undergoes oxidation (acts as the anode).
Cathode (Reduction): $2 \times [AgBr(s) + e^- \rightarrow Ag(s) + Br^-(aq)] \quad E_{cathode}^\theta = +0.07\text{ V}$
Anode (Oxidation): $Fe(s) + 2OH^-(aq) \rightarrow Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2e^- \quad E_{anode}^\theta = -0.88\text{ V}$ (given as reduction potential)
Overall Reaction: $Fe(s) + 2OH^-(aq) + 2AgBr(s) \rightleftharpoons Fe(OH)_2(s) + 2Ag(s) + 2Br^-(aq)$
This matches option (a).
Checking other options:
- $E_{cell}^\theta = E_{cathode}^\theta - E_{anode}^\theta = 0.07 - (-0.88) = +0.95\text{ V}$ (Option b is incorrect).
- Fe is oxidized from $0$ to $+2$ state (Option c is incorrect).
- $E_{cell}^\theta$ is an intensive property, not an extensive one (Option d is incorrect).

stem:
Consider the following two half-cell reactions along with the standard reduction potential given:
$CO_2 + 6H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow CH_3OH + H_2O \quad E^\circ_{red} = 0.02\text{ V}$
$\frac{1}{2}O_2 + 2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2O \quad E^\circ_{red} = 1.23\text{ V}$
A fuel cell was set up using the above two reactions such that the cell operates under the standard condition of 1 bar pressure and 298 K temperature. The fuel cell works with 80% efficiency. If the work derived from the cell using 1 mol of $CH_3OH$ is used to compress an ideal gas isothermally against a constant pressure of 1 kPa, then the change in the volume of the gas, $\Delta V$ is _______ $\text{m}^3$. (nearest integer)
Given: $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$
solution:
In the fuel cell, methanol is oxidized at the anode and oxygen is reduced at the cathode.
Anode: $CH_3OH + H_2O \rightarrow CO_2 + 6H^+ + 6e^- \quad (E^\circ_{ox} = -0.02\text{ V})$
Cathode: $\frac{3}{2}O_2 + 6H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 3H_2O \quad (E^\circ_{red} = 1.23\text{ V})$
Overall cell potential $E^\circ = 1.23 - 0.02 = 1.21\text{ V}$.
The maximum electrical work available from 1 mole of methanol ($n=6$) is $-\Delta G^\circ = nFE^\circ = 6 \times 96500 \times 1.21 = 700660\text{ J}$.
Actual useful work derived with 80% efficiency = $0.8 \times 700660 = 560528\text{ J}$.
This work is done by the cell to compress a gas. By thermodynamics, work done ON the gas is $W = -P_{ext} \Delta V$.
Thus, $560528 = - (1 \times 10^3\text{ Pa}) \times \Delta V$.
$\Delta V = -560.528\text{ m}^3$. Rounded to nearest integer, $\Delta V = -560$.
